section_summary: This section documents the Japanese government's suppression of Dr. Tatsukichi Minobe's 'Emperor organ' constitutional theory and diplomatic repercussions surrounding the sanctity of the Japanese Emperor. It covers bilateral goodwill exchanges, notably the visit of American Veterans of Foreign Wars leaders to Japan and the rejection of state governors' unauthorized letters to Hirohito under federal constitutional guidelines. Finally, it details extensive U.S. State Department and New York City police coordination in response to Japanese Embassy protests against a planned mock trial of Emperor Hirohito organized by anti-war and pro-China groups in New York.

subfiles.about: Reporting the Okada Cabinet's statements and measures suppressing Dr. Minobe's institutional theory of the Emperor.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville (Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: This despatch completes reporting on the Minobe controversy, detailing Cabinet pressure by the military chiefs and the government's October 1 announcement implementing ideological screening in education. An enclosed London Times article by Hugh Byas analyzes the deeper struggle of the military services to preserve their independent prerogative of supreme command against civil parliamentary control.
subfiles.title: Suppression of Dr. Minobe's Constitutional Theory and Government Actions on National Polity (Despatch No. 1501 Enclosure)

subfiles.about: Noting Japanese consular protests in Shanghai against the distribution of Vanity Fair containing a caricature of the Emperor.
subfiles.from: Edwin S. Cunningham (Consul General, Shanghai)
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Vice Consul in Shanghai sought assistance from the American Consulate General and Shanghai Municipal Police to halt distribution of the August issue of Vanity Fair. The American Consulate declined to intervene, noting that police censorship of American periodicals in the International Settlement would be improper and outside their jurisdiction.
subfiles.title: Japanese Efforts to Suppress Vanity Fair in Shanghai (Despatch No. 10294 Extract)

subfiles.about: Transmitting the Japanese Government's second official declaration condemning the Emperor organ theory.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville (Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 1518 forwards an English translation of the Japanese Cabinet's October 15, 1935 declaration explicitly condemning the Emperor organ theory as contrary to Japan's sacred national structure. The statement resulted from compromise negotiations between military leaders and Premier Okada, providing a temporary political truce without immediately forcing the resignations of Baron Ikki or Director Kanamori.
subfiles.title: Controversy over the Institutional Theory of the Japanese Emperor (Despatch No. 1518)

subfiles.about: Summarizing military agitation and government moves against constitutional heresy regarding the Emperor.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville (Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Extracted from Tokyo Periodic Report No. 94, this document outlines continued military pressure following Dr. Minobe's resignation from the House of Peers and the judiciary's decision not to prosecute him. It describes joint Army and Navy demands submitted to Premier Okada calling for the suppression of unorthodox constitutional interpretations and targeting remaining moderates in official posts.
subfiles.title: Steps for the Extermination of Heretical Ideas Concerning the Emperor (Periodic Report No. 94 Extract)

subfiles.about: Sharing published commentary on Japanese-American mutual perceptions regarding the Emperor.
subfiles.from: Sydney Greenbie
subfiles.summary: Author Sydney Greenbie writes to Secretary Cordell Hull recalling past efforts to promote mutual understanding with Japanese representatives regarding the Emperor's status and enclosing his recent publication. The Department courteously acknowledges receipt through Assistant to the Secretary H. A. McBride.
subfiles.title: Correspondence Between Sydney Greenbie and Department of State Regarding Emperor Sensitivity

subfiles.about: Arranging official courtesies for the VFW delegation's goodwill journey to Japan.
subfiles.from: Charles E. Weickhardt (VFW) and Department of State
subfiles.summary: The Veterans of Foreign Wars informs the State Department of Commander-in-Chief James E. Van Zandt's invitation from General Suzuki to attend the Emperor's birthday celebrations in Tokyo. The Department instructs Ambassador Grew in Tokyo to extend appropriate assistance to the visiting American veteran delegation.
subfiles.title: Arrangements for the Visit of VFW Commander-in-Chief Van Zandt to Japan
subfiles.to: Cordell Hull and Joseph C. Grew

subfiles.about: Exchanging formal felicitations on the occasion of the Emperor's birthday.
subfiles.from: President Franklin D. Roosevelt and Emperor Hirohito
subfiles.summary: This subfile contains the draft and transmission of President Roosevelt's annual birthday congratulations to Emperor Hirohito on April 29, 1936. It includes Emperor Hirohito's telegraphic reply of appreciation dispatched from Tokyo on April 30 and referred to the Department of State.
subfiles.title: Exchange of Birthday Messages Between President Roosevelt and Emperor Hirohito
subfiles.to: Emperor Hirohito and President Franklin D. Roosevelt

subfiles.about: Requesting and granting customs courtesies for goodwill gifts brought by returning VFW delegates.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew and Treasury Department
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew telegraphed that the returning VFW delegation was transporting gifts presented by the Japanese Veterans Association and requested customs courtesies upon arrival in Seattle. The State Department liaised with the Treasury Department, which authorized the Collector of Customs at Seattle to grant routine facilities.
subfiles.title: Customs Facilities for Gifts Brought by Returning VFW Delegation
subfiles.to: Secretary of State and Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Reporting the return of unauthorized gubernatorial letters addressed to the Emperor of Japan.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew (Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports that VFW delegate John J. Skillman carried letters of introduction addressed directly to Emperor Hirohito from Governor Hoffman of New Jersey and Governor Sholtz of Florida. Because diplomatic regulations forbid forwarding communications to a foreign sovereign without State Department authorization, the Embassy returned the letters unpresented.
subfiles.title: Letters of Introduction to the Emperor Given by State Governors (Despatch No. 1844)

subfiles.about: Providing a comprehensive account of the VFW delegation's goodwill tour across Japan.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew (Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 1845 reviews the nationwide reception accorded the eight-member VFW delegation led by James E. Van Zandt during their April-May 1936 tour of Japan. Ambassador Grew praises the delegates for their disciplined avoidance of political controversies and highlights public speeches emphasizing peace, anti-war profit initiatives, and friendly international ties.
subfiles.title: Visit to Japan of Representatives of the Veterans of Foreign Wars (Despatch No. 1845)

subfiles.about: Reporting the local celebration of the Japanese Emperor's birthday in Foochow, China.
subfiles.from: Gordon L. Burke (Foochow)
subfiles.summary: Extract from Foochow Periodic Report No. 99 detailing an official reception hosted by Japanese Consul General Toyoichi Nakamura on April 29, 1936 in honor of Emperor Hirohito's birthday. The gathering was attended by foreign dignitaries, missionaries, business representatives, and a Kuomintang provincial party commissioner.
subfiles.title: Japanese Emperor's Birthday Celebration at Foochow (Report Extract)

subfiles.about: Noting the temporary suspension of a Japanese newspaper in Tsingtao over an imperial rescript reference.
subfiles.from: Samuel Sokobin (Tsingtao)
subfiles.summary: A cross-reference sheet recording that a Japanese newspaper published in Tsingtao suspended publication for three days following an objectionable reference to the Emperor's rescript opening the Diet on May 5, 1936.
subfiles.title: Suspension of Japanese Newspaper in Tsingtao (Document File Note)

subfiles.about: Analyzing legal restrictions on unauthorized communications by state governors to foreign rulers.
subfiles.from: Legal Adviser's Office, Department of State (William R. Vallance)
subfiles.summary: This legal memorandum reviews Article 2 of the U.S. Constitution and Section 5 of the Criminal Code (the Logan Act) regarding presidential supremacy over diplomatic intercourse. It suggests advising the governors of New Jersey and Florida to refrain in the future from issuing commissions or letters addressed directly to foreign heads of state.
subfiles.title: Control of the President over Correspondence with Foreign Governments (Legal Memorandum)

subfiles.about: Instructing the Tokyo Embassy to brief the Japanese Foreign Office on federal and local responses to a planned mock trial.
subfiles.from: Department of State (Cordell Hull / R. Walton Moore)
keywords: American Friends of the Chinese People
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 119 instructs the Tokyo Embassy to inform the Japanese Foreign Ministry informally that U.S. authorities lack statutory power to prohibit a mock trial of Emperor Hirohito planned by the American Friends of the Chinese People. The embassy is directed to convey regrets over actions offensive to friendly nations while assuring that police precautions will safeguard Japanese persons and property.
subfiles.title: State Department Instructions Concerning Proposed Mock Trial of the Emperor (Telegram No. 119)

subfiles.about: Recording discussions with Japanese diplomats to prevent sensationalized press reporting to Japan.
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman (Division of Far Eastern Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Eugene H. Dooman documents contacts with Japanese Embassy Counselor Yoshizawa and news agencies regarding press coverage of the New York meeting. Japanese correspondents agreed to withhold reports from Tokyo, and American wire services indicated they had no interest in cabling reports of the affair to Japan.
subfiles.title: Efforts to Prevent News Agency Reports of Mock Trial from Reaching Japan
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs files

subfiles.about: Reporting the Japanese Vice Minister's reaction to American handling of the mock trial issue.
subfiles.from: Erle R. Dickover (Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Tokyo Embassy telegram No. 187 reports that the Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs appreciated the Department's interest and recognized U.S. legal constraints. The Vice Minister urged that news agencies be discouraged from telegraphing reports to Japan, noting that publicity was the primary oxygen for radical organizations.
subfiles.title: Japanese Foreign Office Reaction to Department Instructions (Telegram No. 187)

subfiles.about: Transmitting New York City police reports showing that no mock trial took place at the radical assembly.
subfiles.from: Mayor Fiorello H. LaGuardia and Police Commissioner Lewis J. Valentine
subfiles.summary: Mayor LaGuardia forwards an investigation by NYPD's Criminal Alien Bureau covering the September 17, 1936 meeting at the New School for Social Research. The police report confirms that although anti-Japanese speeches were delivered by Roger Baldwin, Joseph Freeman, and others, no mock trial of Emperor Hirohito was staged, and proceedings conformed to ordinary parliamentary rules.
subfiles.title: New York City Police Report on the Meeting at the New School for Social Research

subfiles.about: Commending Mayor LaGuardia and the New York Police Department for effective monitoring and cooperation.
subfiles.from: Cordell Hull (Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Secretary Hull writes to Mayor LaGuardia thanking him for transmitting the detailed police report and expressing deep appreciation for the cordial and effective cooperation provided by the New York municipal authorities and police department.
subfiles.title: Secretary Hull's Appreciation to Mayor LaGuardia for Police Cooperation
subfiles.to: Fiorello H. LaGuardia (Mayor of New York)

subfiles.about: Preserving radical promotional leaflets announcing the proposed trial and educational courses.
subfiles.from: American Friends of the Chinese People
subfiles.summary: This subfile contains the original printed handbill advertising 'Emperor Hirohito On Trial' at the New School for Social Research, listing accusers and witnesses, alongside a curriculum prospectus for The School for Far Eastern Studies offering evening classes on Modern China and Japan.
subfiles.title: Handbill for Emperor Hirohito Trial and Prospectus for Far Eastern Studies

subfiles.about: Recording initial Japanese Embassy representations concerning the scheduled mock trial.
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman and Seijiro Yoshizawa
subfiles.summary: Counselor Yoshizawa informally informed the State Department of plans by the American Friends of the Chinese People to stage a mock trial of the Emperor and an anti-Japanese demonstration on the Mukden Incident anniversary. Both sides agreed to avoid public disclosures that might magnify the incident or exacerbate popular resentment in Japan.
subfiles.title: Conversation Between Mr. Dooman and Counselor Yoshizawa Regarding Proposed Mock Trial
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs files

subfiles.about: Reporting press announcement of the public trial of the Japanese Emperor in Manhattan.
subfiles.from: Daily Press Clipping
subfiles.summary: A short newspaper clipping titled 'Will Try Mikado On Manchuria Raid' announcing the public trial of Emperor Hirohito scheduled for September 17 at the New School for Social Research, citing witnesses Haru Matsui and Wu Kau-liu.
subfiles.title: Press Clipping: Will Try Mikado On Manchuria Raid

subfiles.about: Transmitting evidence and police findings to the Tokyo Embassy confirming the mock trial did not occur.
subfiles.from: R. Walton Moore (for the Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Instruction No. 1112 transmits to Tokyo Chargé Dickover copies of the protest letter, handbill, and the official New York Police Department report. The instruction confirms for the Embassy's records that the scheduled meeting did not culminate in any trial of the Emperor.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 1112 to Tokyo Transmitting Findings on New School Meeting
subfiles.to: Erle R. Dickover (Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo)

subfiles.about: Detailing high-level consultations between the State Department and Mayor LaGuardia on legal options.
subfiles.from: Maxwell M. Hamilton
subfiles.summary: Maxwell M. Hamilton flew to New York to confer with Mayor LaGuardia regarding preventive measures against the mock trial. LaGuardia explained that municipal and state statutes provided no authority to ban peaceful private gatherings in advance, warning that official attempts at suppression would merely hand radical organizers sensational publicity and drive them into larger venues like Madison Square Garden.
subfiles.title: Consultation with Mayor LaGuardia Regarding the Proposed Mock Trial (Memorandum of Conversation)
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs files

subfiles.about: Documenting Justice Department review finding no federal basis to prohibit the mock trial.
subfiles.from: Maxwell M. Hamilton
subfiles.summary: Hamilton records that Secretary Hull contacted Assistant to the Attorney General Joseph B. Keenan to explore legal grounds for federal intervention. Keenan determined that the Department of Justice had no legal basis to prevent the meeting, citing a comparable municipal precedent involving Benito Mussolini in Cleveland.
subfiles.title: Consultation with Department of Justice on Legal Authority to Halt Mock Trial
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs files

subfiles.about: Conveying official U.S. views and expressions of regret to the Japanese Embassy Counselor.
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman and Seijiro Yoshizawa
subfiles.summary: Dooman informed Yoshizawa of the Department's telegraphic instructions and expressed personal regret over provocations against friendly foreign heads of state. Yoshizawa concurred that governments should avoid dignifying such stunts and expressed appreciation for the proactive, courteous handling shown by the United States.
subfiles.title: Follow-Up Conversation with Counselor Yoshizawa on Government Response to Mock Trial
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs files

subfiles.about: Providing field intelligence from State Department special agents on the New School meeting.
subfiles.from: Special Agent in Charge, New York Division
keywords: American Friends of the Chinese People
subfiles.summary: The New York Division Special Agent reports to Chief Special Agent R. C. Bannerman on the proceedings of the September 17 gathering at the New School for Social Research. The report corroborates that police protection was coordinated for the Japanese Consulate and summarizes the remarks of substitute speakers.
subfiles.title: Report of Special Agent in Charge Regarding New School Meeting Proceedings
